entries.name: Battles on Gensokyo
entries.content:
In Gensokyo, the vast majority of confrontations, including battles, duels, and skirmishes, predominantly take place high above the ground. Typically, combatants engage in intricate danmaku exchanges while airborne, weaving through the colorful barrages of bullets and spells until one is ultimately vanquished, resulting in a dazzling explosion of light that illuminates the sky. These danmaku fights are designed to be non-lethal, allowing participants to showcase their skills without the fear of death; however, they can still cause damage, tearing and breaking clothing or leaving behind bruises as a reminder of the fierce competition. While aerial combat is the standard, there are rare instances where danmaku and spellcard battles unfold on the ground, offering a different dynamic to the encounters.

In Gensokyo, the ability to fly is not just a skill but an essential survival mechanism, particularly for humans who must navigate the dangers posed by Youkai attacks. This aerial agility provides a crucial advantage, enabling them to evade threats and find safety in the skies, where they can momentarily escape the clutches of their adversaries.

entries.name: Spellcards
entries.content:
Spell cards (スペルカード Superukādo) seem to be crucial in the execution of potent, specific magic. When a user enters a spell card trance, both their offensive and defensive abilities appear to be significantly enhanced. In certain instances, the user achieves complete invulnerability for the duration of the trance. Nevertheless, the user is restricted to casting only the spell indicated by the spell card until the trance concludes, which can limit its overall effectiveness.

The concept of spell cards was created by Reimu Hakurei, although there are doubts about the original draft being based on a youkai agreement. The first application of this system occurred during the Scarlet Mist Incident. They were intended to level the playing field for weaker youkai and humans, while also offering youkai a fair method to challenge the Hakurei Shrine in battle. This rationale was particularly highlighted during the Silent Sinner in Blue incident, when Marisa Kirisame persuaded Watatsuki no Yorihime to adopt spell card regulations to ensure fairness in combat and, as Yorihime stated, to avoid violence.

In the context of the Silent Sinner in Blue event, Marisa Kirisame likens spell cards to a standard duel: one must evade their adversaries or face defeat. However, the distinction lies in the notion that "the one who is most beautiful wins. It’s a contest of the mind." Reisen Udongein Inaba elaborates that "beautiful" implies a lack of underhanded tactics. As outlined subsequently, spell cards establish various rules for the duration of a duel, including the equipment utilized, time constraints, conditions for victory and defeat, and specific limitations, especially regarding evasion.

Interestingly, spell cards are not confined solely to magic. For instance, Sanae Kochiya can invoke divine power, while Nitori Kawashiro and Marisa can utilize items like the Mini-Hakkero. Any object that can serve as an offensive weapon qualifies as a spell card, including common household items. Kogasa Tatara employs umbrellas in some of her spell card techniques, while Minoriko Aki utilizes potatoes. The absence of such equipment does not allow for the creation of unique spell cards; for example, without her Hakkero, Marisa would be unable to execute her Master Spark.

Initially, spell cards were depicted as sheets of paper containing descriptions of their associated spells, along with the potential endorsement of the shrine maiden.

entries.name: Danmaku
entries.content:
danmaku is incorporated into the setting itself, where it is essentially a supernatural martial art practiced by the inhabitants of Gensokyo, based on ranged attacks.

Danmaku is a kind of magic exclusive to Gensokyo culture which its user can use to shoot at the rival and damage, if the rival is defeated, they don't die, but will have bruises (Danmaku is not for killing).

Under the spell card rules, danmaku duels are not to the death but are ritualized and aestheticized sparring matches with agreed-upon conditions for winning and losing.

Danmakus can be transformed into other things that can also be used in battles, such as wind, water, or more. In the case of Aya Shameimaru, she uses her Danmaku as wind waves, and as another example, there is Kogasa, which uses her Danmaku to turn in water droplets to shoot. The list of uses of Danmaku in combat is extensive, with more examples being Marisa shooting Danmaku stars, missiles, and lasers; Reimu shooting Danmaku amulets and Needles; Sakuya danmaku knives; Utsuho fireballs, heat waves, lasers;  and more on.

entries.name: Mini-Hakkero
entries.content:
The mini-Hakkero (ミニ八卦炉, "mini-Eight Trigram Furnace" or "mini-Elemental Furnace") is a magical device owned by Marisa Kirisame. it was originally given to Marisa by Rinnosuke Morichika after she stopped living with her parents. The mini-Hakkero takes the shape of a hand-sized octagonal block of wood, with the eight Taoist trigrams inscribed in a circle around its center. The internal components were originally made of iron or steel, but replaced by the mythical hihi'irokane metal after rusting. It is capable of generating immense heat and magical energy--Rinnosuke describes it as capable of reducing a mountain to ashes. Marisa relies on it heavily for research and combat, most notably to power her Master Spark.

In addition to its normal functions, one of the furnace's corners releases a cool breeze, and the hihi'irokane model gleans negative ions from the air (a function copied from a pseudoscientific device from the Outside World, which nevertheless works inside Gensokyo). Rinnosuke also believes that the mini-Hakkero may function as an amulet for protection and good fortune.

During the events of Double Dealing Character the mini-Hakkero was one of the weapons "corrupted", or in other words, brought to life, by the power of the Miracle Mallet.

entries.name: Magician
entries.content:
Magicians (魔法使い mahou-tsukai, which translates to "user of the sorcerous method") and witches (魔女 majo, meaning "sorcerous woman") typically denote individuals believed to have the ability to wield magic. The term ma (魔) originally referred to dark practices, demons, and those who engaged with them, but in contemporary usage, it can encompass any form of Western-style magic, whether benevolent or malevolent.

The label "magician" applies to both a profession and a category of youkai. A human magician has the potential to transform into a magician youkai by delving into magical studies that eliminate their need for sustenance, although some magician youkai are naturally born into this state. Regardless of their origin, the physical form of a magician youkai remains fundamentally human, lacking the enhanced strength and endurance characteristic of many youkai. In fact, numerous magician youkai are quite fragile, even by human standards, due to insufficient physical activity and exposure to harmful magical substances such as arsenic and mercury. A magician youkai is deemed "complete" upon mastering the ability to halt their aging through magic—a capability that historical magicians could only realize in their later years, but which has become increasingly attainable as magical understanding has progressed.

A magician youkai may also emerge when an ordinary object is infused with a significant amount of magical energy, leading to a description akin to golems. An example of this is Narumi Yatadera, who originated as a Jizo statue animated by the potent forces of the Forest of Magic. This kind of magician can be likened to tsukumogami, as they are objects that have gained life; however, their power is derived from magic rather than the unrest of their spirit.

Both human and youkai magicians exhibit remarkable adaptability in their manipulation of spiritual energy. While most beings are confined to the powers they are inherently born with, a magician theoretically can produce nearly any effect, provided they comprehend its mechanics and can formulate an appropriate spell. They do, however, depend to some extent on external sources of magical energy, such as the mushrooms found in the Forest of Magic. The nature of this energy is crucial; for instance, Marisa points out that ice magic is straightforward to perform in winter but becomes challenging in summer without a strongly associated item, like Water Dragon scales. Many magicians tend to have a specific type of magic in which they excel or have a preference for, such as Alice's proficiency with dolls or Byakuren's emphasis on physical enhancement. A magician's residence is often cluttered with books, notes, and artifacts, reflecting the extensive study and effort required to master various spells; as a result, they are commonly perceived as reclusive, scholarly individuals.

entries.name: Onis and Kishin
entries.content:
Oni are jolly youkai who love to drink, feast, and compete with humans in any kind of contest, from simple physical fighting to drinking games. Long ago, when an oni found a human that they liked, they tempted that human into challenging them in any way the human desired. Should the human lose, they were to be abducted. Because normal humans were nowhere near an oni's capabilities, they mostly resorted to sneaky underhanded tactics in order to beat the oni. Tired of being tricked and beaten all the time, the oni swore off humans forever and left for a place beyond human reach, or so the legend says.

In Gensokyo, oni were once the main residents of the Youkai Mountain, and were above tengu and kappa in the hierarchy. They were led by the Big Four of the Mountain. However, they eventually moved into Old Hell sometime after the actual Hell was moved away from the Underworld by the yama. In Hell, oni are lead by the kishin to torture the souls of sinners.

Komachi Onozuka mentions that the oni of current Hell are under control and the ones of Old Hell have too many close relationships with the ghosts of sinners, making them not fond of the idea of leaving to the real Hell anytime soon.

kishin are powerful youkai who reside in Hell. Each kishin chief commands a number of lesser oni in their torment of the souls who fall into Hell, utilizing a wide array of torture devices. When a hermit or celestial has lived too long, a kishin chief is sent to assassinate them, though most of the living believe that the assassin is a shinigami due to misinformation they have spread. According to Hecatia, there are kishin at the top of the organization of Hell that work with yama. It is unknown if these elite kishin are of the same type of kishin that manage Hell's oni or if they are Buddhist wrathful deities.

[Oni (鬼) are fabulous creatures from Japanese folklore, similar to Western demons or ogres. They're almost always depicted as beings with incredible strength and power; physically, two long horns are said to grow from their heads. The earliest folktales of oni generally described them as benevolent creatures able to ward off evil and punish the wicked, but over time, oni began to be seen as cruel, malevolent creatures, content only to destroy. "Oni" in Japanese is sometimes used non-literally to describe beings of similar cruelty, such as vampires (吸血鬼 kyūketsuki, literally "blood-sucking oni").

Kishin (鬼神) is a Japanese word combining the characters for "oni" (鬼) and "god" (神). It usually refers to a wrathful deity, a type of divine being in Buddhism or to an exceptionally powerful oni.]

[Kishins and Onis are Youkais.]

[Onis tradition= The oni in Gensokyo have a very common tradition of kidnapping humans as a way of showing affection.]

entries.name: Gensokyo
entries.content:
Gensokyo (幻想郷 gensoukyou, "Land of Illusions" or "Land of Fantasy") is a secret world, hidden from th Outside world (the outside world is a  world where humans reside). Gensokyo is a secret land where humans and youkais coexist. Its culture vaguely resembles that of feudal Japan, heavily embellished with folkloric elements.

Gensokyo is a remote place, far from any human habitation. In ancient times, this place was densely populated by youkai and those humans who wandered too close would be eaten by them. Most people feared the youkai, but a brave warrior would occasionally rise to defeat them. Some of those brave humans settled in Gensokyo to keep close watch on the youkai. Scientific advancements among the human race further contributed to Gensokyo's growing human minority. Due to this, Yukari Yakumo implemented a plan roughly 500 years ago to restore the power of youkai in Gensokyo by creating a "Barrier that divides Reality and Fantasy" called the Youkai Expansion Project. With the plan's implementation, Gensokyo became a place where it brought in things that have become fantasy outside; in other words, things that were forgotten in the Outside World such as youkai, lost items, and such are paranormally transported into Gensokyo. In 1885 A.D., Gensokyo was again made isolated from the rest of Earth with the creation of the Great Hakurei Barrier. Gensokyo has made next to no attempt at contact with the outside world since its creation. Gensokyo's language is modern Japanese.

Gensokyo, the area encompassed by the Great Hakurei Barrier, is a landlocked territory comprised mainly of forested mountains. Notable geographic features include the Youkai Mountain with communities of kappa at its base, tengu at its peak, and the Moriya Shrine at a lake near the top; the Forest of Magic; the Bamboo Forest of the Lost where Eientei is located; the Misty Lake next to the Scarlet Devil Mansion; the Human Village and adjacent Myouren Temple, which are assumed to be in a fertile valley; the Sanzu River separating Gensokyo from Higan; and the Hakurei Shrine at the east of Gensokyo.

Although passing through the Hakurei Barrier to the Outside World is normally impossible for weaker people, stronger entities are known to be able to pass through. It is also significantly easier for Gensokyo denizens to access domains of gods, demons, and spirits which are not strictly part of Gensokyo itself. These include Higan, the Netherworld, Makai, Heaven, Senkai and the Underworld.

The Youkai Mountain retains the original appearance of Mount Yatsugatake before Konohana-Sakuyahime, the goddess of Mount Fuji, destroyed it. In the outside world today, the remnants of the mountain can be seen as the Yatsugatake mountain range in Yatsugatake-Chūshin Kōgen Quasi-National Park between Nagano and Yamanashi Prefectures, providing a possible indication of where Gensokyo would be located in Japan. Lake Suwa (諏訪湖 Suwa-ko) and Mount Moriya, which Suwako Moriya was named after, are located nearby.

entries.name: Dream World
entries.content:
The Dream World (夢の世界 Yume no Sekai) is a realm accessed through dreams and is governed by Doremy Sweet.

Typically, individuals enter the Dream World while dreaming, where they take on their "dream self."

There is also a physical entrance to the Dream World, known as the "Kaian Passageway #4 (第四槐安通路)," which Reisen Udongein Inaba describes. This passageway is reported to facilitate travel between the Lunar Capital and Gensokyo for the moon rabbits. It has a somewhat cosmic appearance, as noted by Sanae Kochiya, who exclaims, "I'm flying through space!" while both the Moon and Earth can be seen.

The Dream World is often easily recognizable, as it typically resembles a frightening and surreal amusement park, characterized by dark surroundings and ominous colors, essentially creating a valley of strangeness.

entries.name: Hakurei Barrier
entries.content:
The Great Hakurei Barrier (博麗大結界 Hakurei Dai-Kekkai) is the barrier that hides Gensokyo away from the Outside World, and which allows youkai to survive within even when outside humans no longer believe in them. It is known that the Hakurei Shrine is located on the border, and believed that Yukari Yakumo lives somewhere along the border as well (though not near the shrine).

Sometime in the 15th century, the youkai now known as Yukari Yakumo set the groundwork for the barrier with her "Youkai Expansion Project", turning Gensokyo into a haven for youkai by enchanting it to attract the fantastic and repel the mundane.

The Barrier was proposed by Yukari and the other Sages of Gensokyo and erected later in Meiji 18 (CE 1885). Although the Gensokyo Record states that it was made by human priests and later reinforced by youkai. The Gensokyo Record is unreliable, and Yukari is widely acknowledged as the creator of the Barrier. One doubter of this is Yuyuko Saigyouji, who doubts that even Yukari could form such a strong barrier. While the idea was at first highly controversial among youkai and led to much infighting between them, it is now almost universally accepted.

The barrier is so important to Gensokyo that the year of its formation is now marked as the year 0 in the Gensokyo Calendar.

The Hakurei Shrine, which exists on both sides of the border, is supposed to be its only gateway. However, the phenomenon of "spiriting away" can also cause objects and even living beings to slip through the border at random, particularly if they have started to be forgotten by the outside world. For instance, the crested ibis started to become more common in Gensokyo after the Japanese variety were recognized as extinct, and paper started showing up more frequently with the rise of digital storage. Outside humans are not protected by the Spell Card rules and thus can be freely preyed on by youkai, but they may choose to become citizens of the Human Village or request for the Hakurei shrine maiden to send them home.

Even in modern times, it is still possible for youkai, gods and even entire locations (such as the Scarlet Devil Mansion and Moriya Shrine) to pass through the border and enter Gensokyo.

While some youkai (most notably Yukari Yakumo, Nue Houjuu and the zashiki-warashi) have shown the ability to exit Gensokyo and travel to the outside world, it appears that this requires uncommon knowledge, abilities and/or conditions, as other characters seem to think of it as nigh-impossible. It is believed that youkai go on "hunting trips" through the border to gather humans from the outside world as food, disguising the kidnappings as stories of people running away from home, but it is unclear how and when these are performed.

As a "boundary of common sense" the barrier is designed to affect only living things and their creations, while allowing natural forces to pass through (hence the barrier is permeable to sunlight, and Gensokyo's rivers are connected to those of the Outside World). The space on the edges of the barrier is non-Euclidean - humans who attempt to leave the barrier will find themselves encountering the same landmarks over and over, without ever getting any further from where they started.

There are two ways of travelling through the Barrier. True, complete passage can be achieved by punching a hole in the barrier and walking through. However, beings may also enter or leave Gensokyo by being "spirited away", a method which is often only temporary and allows only certain items to be brought inside or outside Gensokyo. Some of these spirited away travellers have little physical presence (sometimes to the point of appearing only as a shadow) and will eventually be pulled back home, remembering their trip as if it were only a dream. In fact at least some of these trips have taken the form of literal dreams, with the traveller's mind returning to their body when they awake. However, it is still possible for a dreamer in the Outside World to bring some objects from Gensokyo to the Outside World and viceversa. Yukari is known for being the one who purposely spirits away humans by causing fluctuations in the barrier.

The barrier is weaker around objects which carry the spiritual energy of the Outside World. Usually this effect is barely noticeable, outside of concentrated sources like the Occult Balls. However, when one of the trees around the Hakurei Shrine was killed, a tree from the Outside World was drawn in to replace it, causing the surrounding area to become distorted. On another occasion Rinnosuke Morichika was briefly drawn into the Outside World due to concentrating on an MP3 player while Reimu was nearby tampering with the barrier.

entries.name: Parsee
entries.content:
Parsee Mizuhashi (水橋　パルスィ Mizuhashi Parusi) is a hashihime, or bridge princess, who guards the "bridge" between the surface world and the Underworld. She is able to control the jealousy in others.

Parsee has wavy blond hair and green eyes, and her skin appears to have pale chartreuse tint to it. She wears a dress which resembles the traditional dresses of Iran's nomadic people, as well as Tocharians depicted in a 6th-century AD fresco from the Kizil Caves; the top is brown with purple borders, with a white criss-cross pattern and a pink sash. The bottom is blue and purple with again the white criss-cross pattern and black with criss-crossed red strings hanging on the bottom edge. The criss-cross patterns are evocative of a truss bridge. She has a pink scarf tied around her neck and pink puffy arm socks.

Parsee used to be a guardian, someone who would watch over those crossing her bridge to make sure they passed between the underground and the surface world safely. However, her own jealousy at those travelers eventually caused her to be able to control feelings of jealousy in others.

The Hashihime (橋姫) is a mythical youkai that appears in various Japanese texts (Most notably the The Tale of Heike). After her husband left her and married another woman, the jealous and enraged Hashihime prays to the gods for revenge. A priest tells her a way: She has to dress herself in red and paint her face with the same color, her hair arranged with seven loops and crowned with a burning brazier, then spend 21 days under the Uji bridge while holding a metal rod. So deep was her rage and jealousy, that she actually did the entire process, becoming a vengeful youkai driven by jealousy that only appears in the vicinity of bridges that cross over water. She appears to loving couples, threatening to kill them both unless they break up right there and then. There is also a famous Noh Play about this mythological creature.

Parsee's manipulation of jealousy: It is an ability from the legend of Hashihime. As a youkai who can be called the very embodiment of jealousy, she is able to manipulate those feelings in others. In relation to humans, it is a dreadful ability that can easily destroy them. She lives off of seeing the lives of those she introduces jealousy into being destroyed by it. This may be the reason she was sealed underground. She herself is deep in her own jealousy.

entries.name: Ran
entries.content:
("Ran Yakumo")= {{Ran Yakumo is the "Kitsune Shikigami" of Yukari Yakumo and the master of the bakeneko shikigami Chen.

Ran is from Kitsune species.

Ran is described as a gentle youkai, unless provoked or when someone in her family is attacked, like Chen (Ran's relationship with Chen is like mother and daughter/guardian and pet, with Ran being a motherly figure). Although Ran is a shikigami, she sometimes "forgets" her position as a servant and acts of her own volition, such as deciding to attack Reimu to avenge Chen (Ran has fear of doing some mistakes, since she know that Yukari will punish her with beating or something worse).

Ran was formerly a resident of the Animal Realm, presumably being one of the many spirits inhabiting it. At one point, disgusted by the beastly ideology that pervaded the place, she fled to Gensokyo. It is unknown when Ran met Yukari and became a youkai-possessing shikigami, but based on her interaction with Yuuma Toutetsu, it was likely after Ran left the Animal Realm.

As Yukari's shikigami, Ran must do whatever Yukari commands her to do, such as doing Yukari's chores or checking the Great Hakurei Barrier around Gensokyo for problems. Apparently, Ran's own shikigami, Chen, is too unreliable to be entrusted with doing chores. Sometimes she might be sent as a messenger, or be entrusted with investigating incidents.

In her spare time, Ran often calculates various things such as the width of the Sanzu River. She may also be seen in the Human Village shopping for tofu.

"Using Shikigami": Ran is an extremely strong shikigami, to the point that she can use shikigami of her own. Her shikigami, Chen, only possesses the wisdom of a child, implying that Ran lacks the level of power that Yukari has with respect to shikigami. While Ran cannot act against Yukari's orders, Chen is capable of disobeying Ran. Because of this, she sometimes has to lure or manipulate Chen with catnip.

"Clear intellect": Ran has super-human intellect equal to that of Yukari's, and excels at mathematics. According to Bohemian Archive in Japanese Red, she was able to formulate and prove an equation for figuring out the width of the Sanzu River. The shikigami of Gensokyo have been often likened to personal computers found in the outside world.

"Miscellaneous": One of Ran's spellcards shows that she is capable of quickly increasing her physical capabilities. As part of Yukari's attacks, Ran typically spins at high speed. Ran is shown to use Chen in a similar way.}}

entries.name: Chen
entries.content:
("Chen")= {{Chen is Ran Yakumo's shikigami, who was guarding the village of Mayohiga. Unfortunately, she could put up little resistance due to being far away from her master.

Chen is from Bakeneko (double tailed cat youkai) species.

Chen is a bakeneko youkai that Ran Yakumo uses as shikigami, but since Ran herself is Yukari's shikigami, she is a "shikigami of a shikigami". When possessed as a shikigami, Chen aquires the fearsome power of a kishin, but since her master is also a shikigami, her ability is fairly low. The possession is removed when she is soaked in water, and since she also hates water as a cat, she is in any case weak to water. Her height is "low" and is capable of human speech. She can use impressive black arts, but only possesses the intellect of a human child. Whether she is possessed or not, her personality and appearance don't change.

"Use of sorcery (while possessed as shikigami)": In shikigami state, Chen becomes extremely dangerous and is able to use various kinds of sorcery. She uses techniques that focus on speed and precise, tricky movements to confuse her opponents, making it very similar to sleight of hand. For example, she could make it appear as if she is dashing to the left, but will then attack from the right instead, moving so quickly that to humans it appears like instant teleportation.[3]

"Surprising people (as bakeneko)": When she becomes a regular bakeneko, she becomes more feral and will resort to more physical attacks like biting and clawing with her long nails. Rather than saying she possesses a special ability to surprise accompanying humans, it is more strongly an implication that she's not able to do anything other than things of this extent. (However, even so, for ordinary humans it is dangerous enough). This is the same ability that Kogasa Tatara has - thus in this aspect, they have mutuality.

Chen serves as a shikigami to Ran Yakumo, and becomes much stronger when her master is present. However, she hates water, and splashing her will dispel the shikigami possession, making her resort to physical attacks. She is also very fond of catnip, and will lose the will to fight if some is scattered to distract her.

Chen has dark brown eyes, brown hair and wears a green mob cap. She has black cat ears, with a gold earring in the left one, and two tails. Her dress is red with a white bow on the collar, with gold trimming and light pink frills at the bottom. The dress has light pink sleeves. She wears socks and has long hot pink fingernails.}}

entries.name: Shikigami
entries.content:
Shikigami (式神) is the term used for the summoned spirits of an "onmyouji", a Japanese sorcerer. Shikigami are used to protect and serve their master, much like the Western concept of the witch's familiar. There are many types of shikigami described in legend, the most common type being enchanted paper cutouts that can produce the illusion of another real-life object.

Shikigami often share a special link to their masters, which may cause their onmyouji to receive sympathetic injuries dealt to the shikigami. Because of this link and the enormous amount of energy needed to maintain shikigami, onmyouji do not usually summon more than one or two shikigami at a time.

Shikigami are entities such as spirits that can be utilized to "possess" a youkai through certain techniques. For example, Ran Yakumo was formerly a denizen of the Animal Realm, and as such she's implied to have been a beast spirit without a physical body, but is now a shikigami used by Yukari Yakumo to possesses the body of a nine-tailed youkai fox. In this role, she is bound to do what Yukari tells her to. Chen, however, is only a part-time shikigami at this time and can have her possession removed by getting doused in water.

entries.name: Zanmu
entries.content:
/// Zanmu Nippaku profile

Zanmu Nippaku (日白 残無 Nippaku Zanmu) was the main antagonist of the Unfinished Dream of All Living Ghost incident. She was formerly a human monk before turning into an oni after falling into hell.

Zanmu Nippaku was formerly a human monk during the Sengoku Jidai period. Zanmu discarded her humanity by absorbing beast-youkai spirits. Sensing her imminent fall to Hell, Zanmu ventured there prematurely. There she transformed into an oni and ruled Hell using her intelligence and charisma. She proposed the relocation of Hell from Former Hell, creating a great amount of resentment from those that stayed behind. Currently she resides in Hell. She is said to command great admiration and respect from the dwellers of Hell.

During the events of Unfinished Dream of All Living Ghost, she uses her ability and influence to manipulate the other protagonists in order to achieve her end goal.

Zanmu is described as the perfect oni according to Suika Ibuki. She has both the strength and intelligence that an oni should be portraying, which made her a "intelligentsia". That said and although she made it for selfish reasons, she is also seen to have a sense of grace, seeking a (relatively) peaceful resolution to the beast wars and to protect Gensokyo from destruction. In this sense, she shares much in common with Reimu, feeling a sense of communality.

Zanmu is not easily upset or angered when the events are not going exactly as she wants. She frequently forgives her bumbling assistant, Hisami, showing she can work with an acceptable error range.

According to Saki, Zanmu is a popular figure in Hell. So much so that Zanmu was able to sway the oni to calm down and let her handle the beast spirits situation.

Zanmu is a crimson-eyed girl with long purple-black hair that reaches to her knees. Her hair is straight at the scalp but becomes wavy at the end. She has two short, pointed horns that are wrapped in red strings that are adorned with a single bead and numerous, smaller strings that look like hair. She wears a green T-shirt, with two coloured borders: the outer-most one is yellow while the innermost one is black lines that aren't attached. The t-shirt's neckline, shoulders, sides and sleeves all have the same rip except for the sides, which are partly sewn together with the same red strings that adorn her horns. She also wears long blue shorts that contain many of her shirt's decorations, the borders, the rips and the red strings partly sewn together on each side. The shorts also seem to be double-layered, one being white underneath the shorts. She sports dark red flip-flops.

/// Zamnu's abilities

Capable of manipulating nothingness: Zanmu has the ability to manipulate nothingness. This causes the victim to lose their desires and motivations. It can be subtle, such as distracting the victim, or outright causing them to lose their will to fight or will to continue investigating. In Unfinished Dream of All Living Ghost, she uses her ability to distract Marisa Kirisame and Sanae from the true cause of the incident. Then, she uses her ability to cause the beast spirits leaders to lose their will to fight. Finally, she uses her ability to convince Reimu to stop her investigation.

While Zanmu is able to manipulate nothingness of her victims, some appear to be less affected than others. Reimu's instincts continued to point to Zanmu as the true culprit and Reimu was not able to be manipulated to accept her plans for "resolving the incident". Similarly, she was unable to stop Mamizou Futatsuiwa from continuing her investigating into the incident. Also, due to Hisami's unpredictable masochism tendencies, Zanmu was not able to control Hisami the way she wanted.

/// Extra Information

Zanmu is basically the queen of hell, and surprisingly she is a "human" which is the main leader of hell.

entries.name: Hisami
Sumireko
entries.content:
Sumireko Usami (宇佐見 菫子 Usami Sumireko) is the main antagonist of Urban Legend in Limbo incident. She's a human from the Outside World with psychic powers (ESP). She is the first president of the Secret Sealing Club.

Sumireko has shown herself to be extremely intelligent, determined, passionate, and hubristic in equal parts. She strongly dislikes the modern society of the outside world due to being dictated by modernized corporations and is much more interested into the occult/fantasy, in the sense of actually being directly involved with it in real life. She goes so far into the occult that it can sometimes endanger her life at times. Sumireko often gets excited of the thrill of danger however.

She describes herself as having been a bit of a loner prior to her arrival in Gensokyo but ever since she started coming to Gensokyo and befriending many inhabitants from there, she considers her discovery of Gensokyo to be the best thing to have happened in her life due to the friendships she's made there. Sumireko seems to hold several contradictory opinions, although it comes off less as hypocrisy, and more as though she hasn't been able to fully make up her mind about certain subjects due to her inexperience of being a teenager. She also tends to use friendly nicknames a lot of her close friends such as Reimu and Marisa.

She also describes herself as being chuunibyou, a term usually used mockingly, with a sense of personal pride, alluding to her psychic powers and other magical abilities. In spite of that pride, she does lament that nobody in the Outside World seems to be able to understand her or her passion about the occult and Gensokyo. This may also be in part due to how highly opinionated she is, espousing her beliefs about the "phoniness" of the Outside World's dominant consumerist culture at the slightest provocation. She also dislikes drugs such as smoking and alcohol likely due to the amount of students in her hometown who would do drugs during flower viewings.

She is a strong psychic, capable of various powers associated with the occult, including but seemingly not limited to levitation, pyrokinesis, hydrokinesis, telekinesis, psychokinesis, and teleportation.

After the events of Urban Legend in Limbo, Sumireko gains the ability to travel to Gensokyo in her dreams through a doppelganger which maintains her "permanent" presence in Gensokyo and is actually also youkai-like. She is able to recall the memories of both the time spent possessing the body of her doppelganger as well as those from her "normal" life in the Outside World, allowing her to live a double-life in both worlds. When this happens, this lead to her dream soul coexisting and even sending objects and eventually humans in Gensokyo to the outer world to lessen the shock of the Great Barrier. According to Yukari, she also strengthening the the barrier as well.

Sumireko has brown eyes and shoulder-length brown hair tied in pigtails. On her head is a black fedora with a white bow along with red-framed glasses. She wears a purple plaid skirt and matching vest (resembling a jumper dress), over a long-sleeved white blouse and a black bolo tie with a clasp shaped like a "Quimbaya airplane". Along with this, she wears white socks with bows and black shoes. Sumireko generally carries Zener cards, a tablet computer marked with a hexagram on the back, a smartphone in a white case with various blue shapes on it, and a light-blue liberator. She also wears white gloves, and a black high-collared cloak with a red interior inscribed with pinkish-white runes, and a series of white lines at the bottom rim of the backside.

Her summer uniform appears nearly identical to her winter one, but with shorter and looser sleeves, no gloves, and a skull in place of the Quimbaya airplane. In Violet Detector, her hair and eyes have a dark red tone instead.

entries.name: Urban Legend in Limbo
entries.content:
Urban Legend in Limbo Incident and Sumireko Usami's Plans:

Urban Legend in Limbo revolved around the mysterious happenings in the Netherworld, specifically concerning the spread of bizarre and unsettling urban legends. These legends aren't merely stories; they manifest as tangible phenomena, capable of affecting the world and its inhabitants.

At the heart of this unsettling situation is Sumireko Usami, a human girl from the Outside World possessing powerful psychic abilities (ESP).  She isn't simply a bystander; she's the main cause of the incident, actively involved in the creation and manipulation of these urban legends.  Her motivations are complex and not entirely malicious, but her actions have far-reaching consequences.

Sumireko's primary goal wasn't world domination or outright destruction. Instead, she seeks to create a world shaped by her own unique understanding of reality.  She believes the existing world is dull and lacks the excitement and wonder found in compelling stories.  To achieve this, she uses her psychic powers to weave and spread urban legends, essentially rewriting reality to better suit her vision.  These legends act as building blocks in her grand plan to reshape the world.

Her methods involve planting seeds of unusual events and manipulating perceptions to make the legends seem more real and impactful. She wasn't directly causing harm, but the chaotic consequences of her actions create problems for others. This makes her more of a chaotic agent than a straightforward villain.

While the details of her ultimate goals remain somewhat ambiguous, it's clear that she desires a world filled with wonder and intrigue, a world where the lines between reality and fiction are blurred. Her actions, while causing problems, stem from a desire to create something more engaging and fantastical than the mundane reality she's experienced.

Adding another layer to her antics is the Secret Sealing Club (or Hifuu Club), a group she founded. They're not your typical book club; they're more like a coven of urban legend enthusiasts. They help spread her stories and add their own creative spins to them. Think of it as her team of mischievous minions, all dedicated to spreading chaos and mayhem. They are also heavily implied to be involved in the events of the game.

In short: Sumireko's not trying to conquer Gensokyo; she's trying to entertain it... in the most delightfully terrifying way possible. She's a quirky, unpredictable character whose actions are driven by curiosity, boredom, and a healthy dose of mischief. She's the ultimate Gensokyo troll, and we wouldn't have it any other way!

entries.name: Cirno
entries.content:
Cirno (チルノ Chiruno) is an ice fairy who first appeared on the second stage of Embodiment of Scarlet Devil. In comparison to other fairies, she is relatively strong; however, compared to the vast majority of Gensokyo's residents, her strength is subpar.

Cirno is a childish, confident fairy who appears to have a superiority complex. She proclaims herself to be "the strongest" on three separate occasions in Phantasmagoria of Flower View. In the game's manual, she is labeled as "9. baka" (⑨. バカ, lit. "9. Idiot").

Her superiority complex makes her say and do things that could be considered "idiotic". In Hidden Star in Four Seasons, when Cirno received power from Okina Matara and was warned that it could be too much for her body to handle, she ignored Okina and just asserted that the power was entirely her own. Okina began to suspect Cirno was intentionally playing the fool, but eventually came to the conclusion that she is just a dumb fairy. In Visionary Fairies in Shrine, Cirno faced Okina once again alongside the rest of Gensokyo's fairies; despite being very clearly outmatched, Cirno insisted that Okina was "bluffing", leading Clownpiece to wonder if she really is just an idiot.

Despite this, Cirno does have some intelligence. She can read and count, showing knowledge of rounding and fractions in Great Fairy Wars. In Phantasmagoria of Flower View's story mode, she was capable of recognizing that she was endangered in her battle against Yuuka. Additionally, when warned by Eiki Shiki that eternity does not truly exist even for fairies, Cirno solemnly reflects on her own mortality and the prospect of being sent to Hell, though Aya Shameimaru manages to talk her into focusing on enjoying the present.

Among other things, she enjoys using her abilities to freeze frogs, then watch them revive while thawing out in the water. However, about one in every three attempts, it fails, resulting in the frog being shattered into pieces.

Cirno has the ability to manipulate cold to the point of being able to freeze water. However, even while saying "manipulate", when coldness is in an omitted state, it seems like her surroundings are chilly even in summer. In battle, she uses this ability to attack others with icicles, huge ice cubes, or wieldable weapons like swords, but also to freeze her opponents or their danmaku. However, despite being able to freeze something hot like flaming danmaku, she is unable to freeze lasers.

How she exactly manipulates cold is unclear, but Reisen Udongein Inaba, in one of her quotes in Touhou Hisoutensoku, speculates that when Cirno does it, she warms up inside as a result. This would mean that she just absorbs the heat in the surroundings instead of "creating" cold from nothing.

Some of Cirno's Spellcards are: Snow Sign "Diamond Blizzard"; Freeze Sign "Perfect Freeze"
"Perfect Freeeeeeeeze!"; Hail Sign "Hailstorm"; Ice Sign "Icicle Fall".

Cirno has aqua-colored eyes and hair. She wears a blue ribbon, light pink blouse, blue jumper dress and seems to be wearing white socks. She also has icicle-shaped wings. Cirno is short like any fairy (around 145 cm tall). Cirno has pale skin.

entries.name: Misty Lake
entries.content:
The Misty Lake (霧の湖 Kiri no Mizuumi) is a large lake located at the foot of the Youkai Mountain. Many fairies and youkai alike appear to gather here, especially during the summertime, given the abundant water. The lake and its environs appear to be the home of Cirno, Daiyousei and Wakasagihime.

Commonly, when someone says "The lake" (湖 mizuumi), it usually refers to the Misty Lake. The water in the lake comes from a river originating from the Youkai Mountain. While the Scarlet Devil Mansion was on an island within Misty Lake as of Embodiment of Scarlet Devil, the mansion would be said to be on a bank next to the lake itself rather than on an island in future installments and written works. At and around noon each day, a strange mist envelops the entire lake, making it difficult to see anything (hence the origin of the name). The origin of this mist is unknown, but it appears that because of the bad visibility, the lake isn't as big as one would think – it would take about an hour to walk the full length around the river, so one can estimate the circumference to be about 3.1 miles (5 km).

Extremely large monster fish live in the lake as well, and can occasionally be caught on nights of the new moon. This has led to the lake being popular amongst anglers who aim to catch such a fish. These fish range from 2 to 5 fathoms (in essence up to 9 meters), with the largest on recording as 10 fathoms (this is believed to be an exaggeration).

A Master of the Lake also lives there. However, his house is so deep down that only fish or amphibians may dive down there.

It is said that creatures can't live in the lake, making it way more clear.
